The render matches the default on every identity-carrying element (ground, accent, type voice, error summary, reference panel); the green accent also leans to the 'recycling = green' association.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: The detector section was empty (0 hits), so nothing in it could have changed the verdicts. Absence of tells is consistent with a clean but plain page; it is not evidence of specificity.

findings.title: Cancelled booking page is still headed 'Booked' and tells the resident to show the reference at the gate
findings.description: On done (cancelled state) the H1 reads 'Booked'; under DR-204117 a red line says 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.', followed immediately by the unchanged default lines 'Show this at the gate, on your phone or on paper…' and 'A reminder will be sent to your mobile the evening before.' The page gives two opposite messages at the same weight.
findings.impact: A resident glancing at the heading and the big reference may take a cancelled booking for a live one and drive to Quarry Road, where they are turned away at the gate.

harm.statement: Residents opening a cancelled booking on /done.html may read 'Booked' plus 'Show this at the gate' and travel to the centre with a booking that is not on the gate's list.

evidence.detail: H1 'Booked'; red status line; then 'Show this at the gate…' and reminder copy

findings.recommendation: Decide what the cancelled state must say first, and let the heading and the reference panel carry that status; drop instructions that only apply to a live booking.

findings.title: Confirmation page does not show the day, slot time or vehicle that was booked
findings.description: done (default) shows only 'Booked', the reference DR-204117, gate instructions and the centre address. The day (Saturday 17 October), the 09:20-09:40 slot, the vehicle and the waste, all shown on confirm, disappear once the booking is made.
findings.impact: The page residents keep on their phone, or print, for the gate does not tell them when to arrive or what vehicle the booking is for.

harm.statement: A resident who books the evening before and opens /done.html in the morning cannot see from it which day and 20-minute slot they booked, and the attendant checking the phone screen at the gate cannot see the vehicle the booking is for.

evidence.detail: no day, time, vehicle or waste anywhere on the page; same at 375-dark

findings.recommendation: Decide which booking facts the gate and the resident need on the kept screen and put them with the reference.

findings.title: 'Few left' slots are pulled out of time order into an unlabelled block above 'Morning'
findings.description: On / the slots tagged 'Few left' (e.g. 08:20, 09:20, 12:00 … 14:20 on Monday 12; 08:20 … 16:40 on Saturday 17) are rendered as a separate first block with no heading, mixing morning and afternoon times. The 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' groups below then skip those times (Morning on Saturday runs 08:00, 09:20, 10:00, 11:00…, with no 08:20 or 08:40).
findings.impact: Residents who want 'Saturday morning' scan the Morning group for an early time; the times they want may sit in the unlabelled block above, so they may conclude it is not available or pick a later slot.

harm.statement: A resident looking under 'Morning' for 08:20 on Saturday 17 does not find it there and may take it for unavailable, because it is listed in the unlabelled 'Few left' block above.

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity is a tag on a slot in its time group or a separate list; if separate, it needs a heading and must not remove the times from their group.

findings.title: Expired-hold confirm keeps 'Book this slot' as the primary action while the slot row shows a bare dash
findings.description: confirm (expired): the error box says 'This slot is no longer available.', the summary's Slot row reads '– · Change slot', yet the only filled button is still 'Book this slot'. The recovery path is the small underlined 'Change slot' link inside the summary.

criteria.name: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

findings.impact: The strongest element on the page points to an action that cannot succeed; the way forward is the weakest element.

harm.statement: A resident whose hold has expired on /confirm.html is likely to press 'Book this slot' again before finding the small 'Change slot' link, slowing re-booking.

findings.recommendation: Decide what the primary action is when the held slot is gone, and make that the one filled button.

findings.title: No identity beyond the council name: the frame is portable to any council booking
findings.description: Header is an outline bin glyph and 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body-size sans; everything else is the category default (pale ground, one green, bordered tiles, error summary, plain reference card). Nothing from the centre's world (the site, the gate, bays, the waste streams residents sort into) appears even quietly on any surface.
findings.impact: Design note: the service reads as a generic form rather than Dunmore's recycling centre; no task harm claimed.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element from the centre's own world that can recur quietly on Operate surfaces (the identity floor), and decide how the reference on done is set so it reads as the thing shown at the gate; keep controls conventional.

findings.title: Wide-width layout leaves the right half empty and the done footer stops short
findings.description: At 1280/1440 forms and the slot grid stop at ~710-820 px in a ~1088 px column, while the Opening days, Your booking and Your reference boxes stretch full width with text in their left half. On done at 1280 the page and white footer end at ~715 px with flat ground below. At 375 '01632 960771' and 'DN4 2XQ' break across lines in the footer and the At the centre card; 'Permit number' sits ~12 px under the vehicle buttons and 'Back to the slots' touches the H1.
findings.impact: Design note on finish; no user harm claimed.
findings.recommendation: Decide the content width per surface so boxes and their text share one measure, keep the footer anchored to the viewport bottom, and keep phone numbers and postcodes unbroken.

findings.title: Day buttons and vehicle buttons use two different looks for the same single-choice job
findings.description: Day choices are outlined boxes with bold green labels and green borders; vehicle choices are separate boxes with regular dark labels and grey borders. DESIGN.md names 'the quiet text button for quick days' and 'the segmented vehicle control', and the render shows neither as described.
findings.impact: Design note: a small coherence drift between steps; no user harm claimed.
findings.recommendation: Decide one single-choice control treatment and record it in DESIGN.md's component list.

strengths: Rules sit beside the controls they govern ('Starts DRC-, then five digits', 'Rubble (up to four bags)', permit info panel), exactly as the brief asks.
Dark theme is composed (lighter mint actions, cards lighter than ground), not inverted, which suits residents who book in dark mode.
One filled button per step and a clear error summary with linked messages.
keep: Keep the plain, gate-attendant voice and the one-filled-button-per-step discipline; add identity without adding controls or noise.
